title: Studentized Cheap Bootstrap: Achieving Higher-Order Coverage Accuracy with Low Computation
summary: The bootstrap is a versatile method for quantifying statistical uncertainty. Among its variants, a popular approach, the studentized bootstrap, provably achieves higher-order coverage error reduction compared to other benchmarks. However, its implementation typically requires an analytical form of the standard error, or otherwise an additional layer of resampling effort which can be computationally expensive.
